stem: Basaltic Lava rocks over Indian Deccan Plateau were formed in which of the following period ?
expl: The origin of rocks of Peninsular India is about 3600 million years old . Before the Carboniferous Period, it was a part of Gondwanaland. It was during the Carboniferous period that coal was formed in the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari basins. During the Cretaceous Period, large scale volcani activity produced the Deccan Trap (the Lava Plateau of India) comprising Lava sheets of several thousand meters in depth. The Deccan Trap originated about 66.25 million years ago.

stem: Meghalaya plateau is the part of –
expl: Meghalaya plateau is an extension of the Indian peninsular plateau. It was separated from the peninsular plateau by Malda Gap. Peninsular plateau is triangular in shape. It extends from plains of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar towards south and encompasses whole of the peninsula.

stem: Extra peninsular mountains of India were formed during :
expl: Extra peninsular mountains of India were formed in Cenozoic Era. Himalayan Ranges are an example of extra peninsular mountains of India.

stem: Why is Dhanbad the most densely inhabited district of Chotanagpur plateau ?

options.label: a
options.text: Fertile soil and irrigational facilities by canals from the Damodar.

options.label: b
options.text: Availability of coal, iron ore, mica, copper etc.

options.label: c
options.text: Development of mining industries and industriali-zation.

expl: Dhanbad comes under Chotanagpur plateau which is famous for coal mining and has some of the largest mines in India. Red soil is found in most of its region which is not useful for agriculture. The availability of coal, iron ore, mica etc. is not a good reason for population density.

Chota Nagpur Plateau covers much of Jharkhand as well as adjacent parts of Odisha, West Bengal, Bihar and Chhattisgarh. The Chotanagpur Plateau extends over an area of approximately 86239 sq.km. Chotanagpur consists of a series of plateaus at different levels of elevation. In the Central Western portion, the 'Patland' extended with a height of about 1100 m. Here, the sharp break in slope is marked by steep scarps. Hence it is a front sloping.

stem: Which plateau lies between the Aravalli and the Vindhya ranges?
expl: Malwa plateau spreads over an area of 150000 sq .km with a length of 530km and a width of 390 km. Its northern end is determined by Aravalli, southern end by the Vindhya range and eastern border by Bundelkhand plateau.

stem: The southern part of the Vindhyan Scarpland is called:
expl: The southern part of the Vindhyan Mountain Range is called the Bhander plateau. In the northern part of Madhya Pradesh, behind the back slopes of the Vindhyachal, there are vast plains, low-height hills and valleys, while the southern region consists of these features. The Bhander plateau is known for its steep and rugged terrain and is recognized as a part of the Vindhya Mountains.

stem:
Consider the following statements about Peninsular plateau.
1. Rising from the height of 150 m above the river plains up to an elevation of 600-900 m is the irregular triangle known as the Peninsular plateau.
2. Delhi ridge in the northwest, the Rajmahal hills in the east, Gir range in the west and the Cardamom hills in the south constitute the outer extent of the Peninsular plateau.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
expl: Peninsular Plateau Rising from a height of 150 m above the river plains upto an elevation of 600-900 m is the irregular triangle known as the peninsular plateau. Delhi ridge in the northwest, (extension of the Aravalis), the Rajmahal hills in the east, Gir range in the west and the Cardamom hills in the south consitute the outer extent of the Peninsular plateau. However, an extension of this is also seen in the northeast, in the form of Shillong and Karbi - Anglong plateau. The peninsular India is made up of a series of patland Plateaus such as the Hazaribagh plateau, the Palamu plateau, the Ranchi plateau, the Malwa plateau, the Coimbatore plateau and the Karnataka pleteau etc. This is one of the oldest and the most stable landmasses of India. The general elevation of the plateau is from the west to the east, which is also provend by the pattern of flow of rivers.

stem:
What are not true about the Peninsular Plateau?
1. Height of this plateau is approximately 1000-1500 meters.
2. Height of this plateau generally decreases from West to East.
3. On its East there are Gir Range and on West there are Rajmahal Hills.
expl: The peninsular plateau rises from a height of 150m above. The river plains up to an elevation of 600-900m, form the irregular triangle known as the Peninsular Plateau. Delhi ridge in the northwest (extension of Aravalis), the Rajmahal hills in the east, Gir range in the west and the Cardamom hills in the south constitute the outer extent of the Peninsular Plateau. The height of this plateau generally decreases from West to East. So statements (1) and (3) are incorrect.
